# diagramkit — Full Reference

> Diagram rendering CLI & library. Converts .mermaid, .excalidraw, .drawio, and Graphviz .dot/.gv/.graphviz files to SVG/PNG/JPEG/WebP/AVIF with automatic light/dark mode support and WCAG color contrast optimization.

## Installation

All rendering engines (mermaid, excalidraw, draw.io, graphviz) are bundled:

```bash
npm add diagramkit
npx diagramkit warmup
```

For raster output — PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF (optional):

```bash
npm add sharp
```

### Repo Bootstrap For Agents

Use `node_modules/diagramkit/REFERENCE.md` (then `node_modules/diagramkit/ai-guidelines/usage.md`) as the first files to read when adding diagramkit to an existing repository. Always anchor on the locally installed version under `node_modules/`, not a globally installed `diagramkit` CLI.

Recommended setup steps:

1. `npm add diagramkit`.
2. Add `"render:diagrams": "diagramkit render ."` to `package.json`.
3. Create `diagramkit.config.json5` only if the repository needs non-default behavior (`npx diagramkit init --yes` wires up the JSON Schema for editor autocomplete).
4. Install the diagramkit-* agent skills — default path is the CLI itself:
   `npx diagramkit skills install`
   It writes thin pointer SKILL.md files at `.agents/skills/diagramkit-*` (with mirrors under `.claude/skills/`, `.cursor/skills/`, `.codex/skills/`, `.continue/skills/` for detected harnesses) that defer to the bundled originals — version-pinned, idempotent, sweeps orphaned stubs. Flags: `--dir <path>`, `--harness <list>`, `--only <name>...`, `--check`, `--dry-run`, `--json`.
5. Run `npx diagramkit warmup` unless the repository is Graphviz-only.

> The diagramkit npm package no longer ships its own `--install-skill` flag; the default skill installer is now the `diagramkit skills install` subcommand (see [Skills Install Command](#skills-install-command) below). The standalone [`skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) CLI (`npx skills add sujeet-pro/diagramkit`) remains supported as an alternative when you specifically want skills that update independently of the installed `diagramkit`, and stay current via `npx skills update`.

## CLI Reference

### Commands

```
diagramkit render <file-or-dir> [options]            Render diagram file(s) to images
diagramkit <file-or-dir> [options]                   Alias for "diagramkit render"
diagramkit validate <file-or-dir> [--recursive]      Validate generated SVGs for img-tag compatibility
                                  [--json] [--scope-dir <name>]
                                  [--fail-on <CODE,...>] [--fail-on-severity <warn|error>]
diagramkit skills install [options]                  Install versioned-pointer skill stubs
                                                      (.agents/skills + harness mirrors)
diagramkit skills                                    Show skills subcommand help
diagramkit warmup                                    Pre-install Playwright chromium browser
diagramkit doctor [--json]                           Validate runtime dependencies and environment
diagramkit init [--ts] [--yes]                       Create config file (JSON5 or TypeScript)
diagramkit                                           Interactive picker (TTY only)
diagramkit --version                                 Show version
diagramkit --help                                    Show help
diagramkit --agent-help                              Output full reference for LLM agents (this file)
diagramkit --interactive / -i                        Force interactive wizard (TTY required)
diagramkit --no-interactive                          Disable interactive wizard (CI / agents)
diagramkit --yes / -y                                Alias for --no-interactive
```

### Render Options

```
--format <formats>       Output formats, comma-separated (default: svg)
                         e.g. --format svg,png or --format png,webp,avif
--theme <light|dark|both> Theme variants to render (default: both)
--scale <number>         Scale factor for raster output (default: 2)
--quality <number>       JPEG/WebP/AVIF quality 1-100 (default: 90)
--force                  Re-render all, ignore manifest cache
--watch                  Watch for file changes and re-render
--no-contrast            Disable dark SVG contrast optimization
--type <type>            Filter: mermaid | excalidraw | drawio | graphviz
--output <dir>           Custom output directory (all outputs go here)
--config <path>          Path to config file (skip auto-discovery)
--output-dir <name>      Output folder name (default: .diagramkit)
--manifest-file <name>   Manifest filename (default: manifest.json)
--no-manifest            Disable manifest tracking
--same-folder            Output in same folder as source files
--output-prefix <string> Prefix for output filenames (default: '')
--output-suffix <string> Suffix for output filenames (default: '')
--dry-run                Show what would be rendered without rendering
--plan                   Show stale plan with reasons (directory mode)
--strict-config          Fail on config warnings/invalid values
--strict                 Exit non-zero on any single render failure
--max-type-lanes <1-4>   Max concurrent engine lanes in batch render
--log-level <level>      Logging verbosity: silent/error/warn/info/verbose (default: info)
--quiet                  Suppress informational output, only show errors
--json                   Output results as JSON (for CI/scripting)
--interactive / -i       Force the interactive wizard (TTY only)
--no-interactive         Disable the interactive wizard (CI / agents)
--yes / -y               Alias for --no-interactive
```

### Validate Command

```
diagramkit validate <file-or-dir> [--recursive] [--json]
                     [--scope-dir <name>] [--fail-on <CODE,...>] [--fail-on-severity <warn|error>]
```

Validates generated SVG files for structural correctness, `<img>`-tag
renderability, and WCAG 2.2 AA text contrast. Checks every `.svg` in scope for:

- empty file or missing `<svg>` root
- missing `xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"`
- missing `width`/`height` AND no `viewBox` (silent layout failure under `<img>`)
- embedded `<script>` tags (browsers block scripts in SVGs loaded via `<img>`)
- `<foreignObject>` warnings (does not render in all contexts; for Mermaid, set `htmlLabels: false`)
- external `href`/`xlink:href` resources (blocked under `<img>`)
- 50 MB size warning (likely renders slowly)
- low-contrast text (`LOW_CONTRAST_TEXT`, warning) — text/background pairs that fall below the WCAG 2.2 AA threshold of 4.5:1 (normal) or 3:1 (large text)
- extreme aspect ratio (`ASPECT_RATIO_EXTREME`, warning) — rendered SVG width/height ratio outside `[1:1.9, 3.3:1]` (default band; configurable via `SvgValidateOptions.aspectRatio`). Diagrams overflowing typical doc widths (~650–800 px) lose ~39% text legibility when scaled down. Suggestion includes engine-specific fixes: flip Mermaid directives, set `mermaidLayout: { mode: 'auto' }`, split into multiple diagrams, or swap engine.
- overly wide viewBox (`SVG_VIEWBOX_TOO_WIDE`, warning) — calibrated for a ~500px content column with up to 1.5x downscale; disable with `--no-max-width` or raise the threshold with `--max-width <px>`.

Without `--recursive`, only files in the top level of the target directory are
scanned. Exits non-zero when any file fails (or when a policy flag below promotes
a warning to fatal). The same checks run automatically as a post-render gate
inside `diagramkit render`.

**Policy flags** — narrow scope or promote issues to fatal, layered on top of the
baseline (any `error`-severity issue always fails):

```
--scope-dir <name>              Only consider SVGs under a directory named <name> (e.g.
                                 diagrams), skipping hand-authored assets elsewhere in the
                                 tree. No-op when the target is a single file.
--fail-on <CODE,...>            Promote specific issue codes to fatal. Unknown/misspelled
                                 codes are dropped with a warning, not a hard failure.
--fail-on-severity <warn|error> Fail if any issue at or above this severity exists
                                 ("warn" also accepts "warning").
```

Known issue codes (case-insensitive on `--fail-on`): `EMPTY_FILE`, `MISSING_SVG_TAG`,
`MISSING_SVG_CLOSE`, `MISSING_WIDTH`, `MISSING_HEIGHT`, `NO_VISUAL_ELEMENTS`,
`CONTAINS_SCRIPT`, `CONTAINS_FOREIGN_OBJECT`, `MISSING_XMLNS`, `EXTERNAL_RESOURCE`,
`INVALID_VIEWBOX`, `SVG_TOO_LARGE`, `LOW_CONTRAST_TEXT`, `ASPECT_RATIO_EXTREME`,
`SVG_VIEWBOX_TOO_WIDE`.

With `--json`, the command emits a **versioned envelope** (`schemaVersion: 1`):

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "command": "validate",
  "target": { "kind": "file|directory", "path": "/abs/path" },
  "files": 12,
  "valid": 10,
  "invalid": 2,
  "policy": { "scopeDir": null, "failOnCodes": [], "failOnSeverity": null },
  "promoted": [{ "code": "LOW_CONTRAST_TEXT", "severity": "warning", "count": 1 }],
  "failed": true,
  "results": [{ "file": "...", "valid": false, "issues": [] }]
}
```

`policy` echoes the effective flags for this run; `promoted` lists warning-severity
issues that a `--fail-on`/`--fail-on-severity` flag elevated to fatal (errors are
never listed here — they already fail via the baseline); `failed` is the overall
exit disposition. JSON schema: `diagramkit/schemas/diagramkit-cli-validate.v1.json`
(exported from the npm package).

Exit codes: `0` = success, `1` = error (render failure, unknown command, etc.)

JSON schema for `render --json` shipped at `diagramkit/schemas/diagramkit-cli-render.v1.json` and exported from the npm package.

### Skills Install Command

```
diagramkit skills install [--dir <path>] [--harness <list>] [--only <name>...]
                           [--check] [--dry-run] [--json]
diagramkit skills                                    Show help (no subcommand)
```

Writes versioned-pointer skill stubs into a repo. For every skill shipped at
`node_modules/diagramkit/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` it writes a canonical pointer at
`.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` plus thin mirrors under each detected/requested
harness (`.claude/skills`, `.cursor/skills`, `.codex/skills`, `.continue/skills`).
Stubs never copy the skill body — they point at the version-pinned original in
`node_modules`, so every agent reads the skill matching the installed diagramkit.
The stub carries an HTML-comment version marker
(`<!-- diagramkit-skill-pointer: pkg=diagramkit version=<v> generator=diagramkit@<v> -->`)
so re-runs are idempotent (`created`/`updated`/`unchanged`) and drift is detectable.

```
--dir <path>              Target repo directory (default: current directory)
--harness <list>          claude,cursor,codex,continue (repeatable or comma-separated;
                           default: auto-detect from existing .claude/.cursor/.codex/.continue
                           dirs — .agents is always written)
--only <name>...          Restrict to specific skills (repeatable or comma-separated);
                           names match with or without the "diagramkit-" prefix
--check                   Verify only — exit nonzero on any missing/stale/orphaned stub,
                           write nothing
--dry-run                 Show what would change without writing
--json                    Emit a machine-readable result ({ schemaVersion: 1,
                           command: "skills-install", packageRoot, version, mode,
                           harnesses, skills, actions, ok })
```

Orphan sweep: a managed stub (`diagramkit-*` namespace, carries the marker) whose
skill no longer ships is reported as `orphaned` under `--check` and deleted under
plain `install` — but only within the `diagramkit-*` namespace, and only stubs the
tool actually generated (a hand-authored `diagramkit-custom/` without the marker,
or any non-namespaced skill like `prj-foo/`, is never touched).

```bash
npx diagramkit skills install                       # install/refresh
npx diagramkit skills install --harness claude,cursor
npx diagramkit skills install --only mermaid --only review
npx diagramkit skills install --dry-run
npx diagramkit skills install --check --json         # CI drift gate
```

Programmatic equivalents are not part of the package's public `exports` map;
`installSkills()` and friends live in the diagramkit repo's own `cli/skills-install.ts`
and back this subcommand only.

### Examples

```bash
diagramkit render .                                  # Render all in cwd
diagramkit render flow.mermaid                       # Single file
diagramkit render dependency.dot                     # Single Graphviz file
diagramkit render ./docs                             # Directory of diagrams
diagramkit render . --format png --theme light       # Raster for email/Confluence
diagramkit render . --format svg,png                 # Multi-format in one pass
diagramkit render . --watch                          # Watch mode
diagramkit render . --format webp --quality 85       # WebP with custom quality
diagramkit render . --type drawio                    # Only draw.io files
diagramkit render . --theme dark --no-contrast       # Raw dark output
diagramkit render . --config ./custom.config.json5   # Explicit config file
diagramkit render . --output ./build/images          # Custom output directory
diagramkit render . --plan --json                    # Stale plan with reasons
diagramkit doctor --json                             # Environment diagnostics
```

### JSON Envelope Contract (v1)

`--json` output is versioned:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "command": "render",
  "target": { "kind": "file|directory", "path": "/abs/path" },
  "phase": "dry-run|execute",
  "options": {},
  "result": {}
}
```

Legacy root-level JSON objects are deprecated in this pre-release line.

### Format Guidance

Prefer SVG by default for rendered diagrams.
Use raster formats (PNG/JPEG/WebP/AVIF) only when the destination explicitly needs them,
especially email or Confluence embeds.

## Output Convention

Rendered images go to a `.diagramkit/` hidden folder next to each source file:

```
source.mermaid → .diagramkit/source-light.svg + .diagramkit/source-dark.svg
```

Output naming pattern: `{prefix}{name}{suffix}-{theme}.{format}`
Configurable via config.outputDir, config.sameFolder, config.outputPrefix, config.outputSuffix.

## JavaScript API

### Workflow Patterns (Agent-Oriented)

1) **Batch render for docs repos**
- Use `renderAll({ dir: '.', formats: ['svg'] })`
- Call `dispose()` at the end of scripts/CI jobs

2) **Multi-format publishing pipeline**
- Render once with `renderAll({ formats: ['svg', 'png', 'webp'] })`
- SVG is rendered first, rasters are converted from SVG

3) **Watch mode during authoring**
- Use `watchDiagrams({ dir: '.', renderOptions: { formats: ['svg'] } })`
- Keep process running; fix file and save to retry on failures

4) **Custom build-tool integration**
- Use `findDiagramFiles()` + `filterStaleFiles()` + `renderDiagramFileToDisk()`
- Update tracking with `updateManifest()` and cleanup with `cleanOrphans()`

### API Selection Guide

| Use case | API |
| --- | --- |
| Render from string in memory | `render()` |
| Render one file in memory | `renderFile()` |
| Render one discovered file to disk | `renderDiagramFileToDisk()` |
| Render a directory tree to disk | `renderAll()` |
| Live re-render on save | `watchDiagrams()` |

### Core Functions

```ts
import { render, renderFile, renderAll, renderDiagramFileToDisk, watchDiagrams } from 'diagramkit'
```

  render(source: string, type: DiagramType, options?: RenderOptions): Promise<RenderResult>
    Render a diagram from source content string.

  renderFile(filePath: string, options?: RenderOptions): Promise<RenderResult>
    Render a diagram from a file path on disk. Detects type from extension.

  renderAll(options?: BatchOptions): Promise<RenderAllResult>
    Batch render all diagrams in a directory tree. Outputs go to .diagramkit/ folders.
    Returns { rendered: string[], skipped: string[], failed: string[], failedDetails: RenderFailureDetail[] }.

  renderDiagramFileToDisk(file: DiagramFile, options?): Promise<string[]>
    Render a single file to disk with all format variants. Returns written filenames.

  watchDiagrams(options: WatchOptions): () => Promise<void>
    Watch for diagram file changes and re-render. Returns cleanup function.

  createRendererRuntime(): RendererRuntime
    Create an isolated runtime with its own BrowserPool (non-singleton lifecycle).

### Conversion

```ts
import { convertSvg } from 'diagramkit'         // also from 'diagramkit/convert'
```

  convertSvg(svg: Buffer | string, options: ConvertOptions): Promise<Buffer>
    Convert SVG to raster format (PNG/JPEG/WebP/AVIF) using sharp.
    sharp is dynamically imported — only required when called.

### Engine Metadata

```ts
import { ENGINE_PROFILES, getEngineProfile, defaultMermaidDarkTheme } from 'diagramkit'
```

  ENGINE_PROFILES: ReadonlyArray<EngineProfile>
    Static metadata for every supported diagram engine — `type`, `browserPool`
    (true if the engine renders inside the BrowserPool, false if WASM/native),
    and lane/scheduling hints. Iterate this instead of hard-coding the engine
    list when building dashboards or per-engine tooling.

  getEngineProfile(type: DiagramType): EngineProfile
    Lookup helper for a single engine.

  defaultMermaidDarkTheme: MermaidThemeVariables
    Built-in Mermaid `themeVariables` map used for the default `-dark` SVG.
    Re-exported so consumers customizing Mermaid via `mermaidConfig` can
    extend (rather than replace) the theme. Includes WCAG-AA sequence
    `autonumber` and xychart-beta axis text colors.

  defaultMermaidLightTheme: MermaidThemeVariables
    Built-in Mermaid `themeVariables` overrides layered on the `default`
    theme for the `-light` SVG (currently the WCAG-AA sequence `autonumber`
    digit color). MermaidThemeVariables = Record<string, string |
    Record<string, string>> (nested for sections like `xyChart`).

### Errors

```ts
import { DiagramkitError, type DiagramkitErrorCode } from 'diagramkit'
```

  DiagramkitError extends Error
    Every error thrown by the public API is an instance of this class.
    Inspect `error.code` (`DiagramkitErrorCode`) for machine-readable handling.
    Codes match the CLI `failedDetails[].code` strings:
      UNKNOWN_TYPE, RENDER_FAILED, MISSING_DEPENDENCY, CONFIG_INVALID,
      BROWSER_LAUNCH_FAILED, BUNDLE_FAILED.

### Configuration

```ts
import { defineConfig, loadConfig, getDefaultConfig, getFileOverrides } from 'diagramkit'
```

  loadConfig(overrides?, dir?, configFile?, options?): DiagramkitConfig
    Load merged config: defaults → global (~/.config/diagramkit/config.json5)
    → env vars (DIAGRAMKIT_*) → local (diagramkit.config.json5 or .ts, walks up) → overrides.
    Pass configFile to load a specific file instead of auto-discovery.

  defineConfig(config): Partial<DiagramkitConfig>
    Identity helper for TypeScript autocomplete in config files.

  getDefaultConfig(): DiagramkitConfig
    Returns built-in default configuration values.

  getFileOverrides(filePath, config?, rootDir?): FileOverride | undefined
    Resolve per-file overrides for a given file path from config.overrides.
    Matches exact filename, relative path, or glob patterns.

### Browser Lifecycle

```ts
import { warmup, dispose } from 'diagramkit'
```

  warmup(): Promise<void>
    Pre-warm the browser pool (launches Chromium).

  dispose(): Promise<void>
    Explicitly dispose the browser pool and close Chromium.

### Utilities (diagramkit/utils)

```ts
import { findDiagramFiles, filterByType, getDiagramType, readManifest, atomicWrite } from 'diagramkit/utils'
```

  findDiagramFiles(dir: string, config?): DiagramFile[]
    Recursively find all diagram source files. Skips hidden dirs and node_modules.

  filterByType(files: DiagramFile[], type: DiagramType, config?): DiagramFile[]
    Filter diagram files by resolved diagram type.

  getDiagramType(filename: string, map?): DiagramType | null
    Resolve diagram type from a filename. Tests longest extensions first.

  getExtensionMap(overrides?): Record<string, DiagramType>
    Get the full extension-to-type mapping, merged with optional overrides.

  getAllExtensions(map?): string[]
    Return all known extensions.

  getExtensionsForType(type: DiagramType, map?): string[]
    Return extensions that map to a given diagram type.

  readManifest(sourceDir, config?): Manifest
    Read the manifest for a source directory.

  isStale(file, formats?, config?, theme?, manifest?): boolean
    Check if a file has changed since last render.

  filterStaleFiles(files, force, formats?, config?, theme?): StaleFile[]
    Filter to only files that need re-rendering.

  getDiagramsDir(sourceDir, config?): string
    Get the output directory path.

  ensureDiagramsDir(sourceDir, config?): string
    Get/create the output directory.

  atomicWrite(path, content: Buffer): void
    Atomic write (.tmp + rename).

### Color Utilities (diagramkit/color)

```ts
import { postProcessDarkSvg, hexToRgb, rgbToHsl, hslToHex, relativeLuminance } from 'diagramkit/color'
```

  postProcessDarkSvg(svg: string): string
    Fix dark SVG contrast by darkening high-luminance fills while preserving hue.

### SVG Validation (diagramkit/utils + diagramkit/validate)

```ts
import {
  validateSvg, validateSvgFile, validateSvgDirectory, formatValidationResult,
} from 'diagramkit/utils'
```

  validateSvg(svg: string, filePath?: string, options?: SvgValidateOptions): SvgValidationResult
    Structural + WCAG 2.2 AA contrast validation of an SVG string.

  validateSvgFile(filePath: string, options?: SvgValidateOptions): SvgValidationResult
  validateSvgDirectory(dir: string, options?: { recursive?: boolean } & SvgValidateOptions): SvgValidationResult[]

  formatValidationResult(result: SvgValidationResult): string
    Human-readable formatter used by `diagramkit validate`.

  SvgValidateOptions:
    checkContrast?: boolean       // Default: true. Set false for hand-authored sources with translucent fills.
    backgroundOverride?: string   // Default: inferred from `-light` / `-dark` filename suffix.

## TypeScript Interfaces

### Types

```ts
type DiagramType = 'mermaid' | 'excalidraw' | 'drawio' | 'graphviz'
type OutputFormat = 'svg' | 'png' | 'jpeg' | 'webp' | 'avif'
type Theme = 'light' | 'dark' | 'both'
```

### DiagramFile

```ts
interface DiagramFile {
  path: string       // Absolute path to source file
  name: string       // Filename without extension
  dir: string        // Directory containing the file
  ext: string        // File extension (e.g. .mermaid, .mmd, .excalidraw, .drawio, .dot, .gv)
}
```

### RenderOptions

```ts
interface RenderOptions {
  format?: OutputFormat           // Default: 'svg'
  theme?: Theme                   // Default: 'both'
  quality?: number                // JPEG/WebP/AVIF quality 1-100. Default: 90
  scale?: number                  // Scale for raster output. Default: 2
  contrastOptimize?: boolean      // Dark SVG contrast fix. Default: true
  mermaidDarkTheme?: MermaidThemeVariables   // Custom dark theme variables
  mermaidLightTheme?: MermaidThemeVariables  // Custom light theme variables
  mermaidLayout?: MermaidLayoutOptions       // Per-call mermaid aspect-ratio rebalance
  config?: Partial<DiagramkitConfig>
  logger?: Logger             // Optional logger for non-fatal warnings
  pool?: BrowserPool          // Optional isolated pool instance
}
```

### RenderResult

```ts
interface RenderResult {
  light?: Buffer     // Light theme output (SVG string as Buffer, or raster binary)
  dark?: Buffer      // Dark theme output
  format: OutputFormat
  width?: number     // SVG width in pixels (SVG output only)
  height?: number    // SVG height in pixels (SVG output only)
}
```

### RenderAllResult

```ts
interface RenderAllResult {
  rendered: string[]   // Files that were rendered
  skipped: string[]    // Files skipped (unchanged, manifest cache hit)
  failed: string[]     // Files that failed to render
  failedDetails: RenderFailureDetail[] // Structured file/code/message diagnostics
  metrics?: {
    durationMs: number
    lanesUsed: number
    countsByType: Partial<Record<DiagramType, { rendered: number; failed: number }>>
  }
}

interface RenderFailureDetail {
  file: string
  message: string
  code: 'UNKNOWN_TYPE' | 'RENDER_FAILED' | 'MISSING_DEPENDENCY' | 'CONFIG_INVALID' | 'BROWSER_LAUNCH_FAILED' | 'BUNDLE_FAILED'
}
```

### BatchOptions

```ts
interface BatchOptions extends RenderOptions {
  dir?: string           // Root directory to scan. Default: cwd()
  force?: boolean        // Force re-render, ignoring manifest. Default: false
  type?: DiagramType     // Filter to specific diagram type
  formats?: OutputFormat[] // Multiple output formats. Overrides format.
  logger?: Logger
  logLevel?: LogLevel    // Logging verbosity. Default: 'info'.
  progress?: boolean     // Show per-file progress logs during batch rendering
  maxConcurrentLanes?: number // 1-4, default 4
  includeMetrics?: boolean
}
```

### WatchOptions

```ts
interface WatchOptions {
  dir: string                              // Root directory to watch
  onChange?: (file: string) => void         // Callback after render
  renderOptions?: RenderOptions & { formats?: OutputFormat[] }
  config?: Partial<DiagramkitConfig>
  configFile?: string                       // Explicit config file path
  strictConfig?: boolean
  pool?: BrowserPool
  debounceMs?: number                      // Debounce time for file events. Default: 200ms
  usePolling?: boolean                     // Chokidar polling mode (useful for network volumes/containers)
  pollingInterval?: number                 // Polling interval in ms when usePolling=true
  logger?: Logger
  logLevel?: LogLevel                      // Logging verbosity. Default: 'info'.
}

type LogLevel = 'silent' | 'error' | 'errors' | 'warn' | 'warning' | 'warnings' | 'info' | 'log' | 'verbose'

interface Logger {
  log: (message: string, ...args: unknown[]) => void
  warn: (message: string, ...args: unknown[]) => void
  error: (message: string, ...args: unknown[]) => void
}

type DiagramkitErrorCode = 'UNKNOWN_TYPE' | 'RENDER_FAILED' | 'MISSING_DEPENDENCY' | 'CONFIG_INVALID' | 'BROWSER_LAUNCH_FAILED' | 'BUNDLE_FAILED'

class DiagramkitError extends Error {
  code: DiagramkitErrorCode
}
```

### ConvertOptions

```ts
interface ConvertOptions {
  format: 'png' | 'jpeg' | 'webp' | 'avif'
  scale?: number         // Scale multiplier for SVG rasterization. Default: 2
  quality?: number       // JPEG/WebP/AVIF quality 1-100. Default: 90
  png?: PngEncoderOptions    // Sharp PNG encoder overrides, merged on { compressionLevel: 9, effort: 10 }
  webp?: WebpEncoderOptions  // Sharp WebP encoder overrides, merged on { effort: 6 }
  avif?: AvifEncoderOptions  // Sharp AVIF encoder overrides, merged on { effort: 6 }
}
```

### OptimizeOptions

```ts
interface OptimizeOptions {
  // Run SVGO + Mermaid CSS pruning on every rendered SVG before it is written.
  // Preserves viewBox, width/height, role/aria-*/<title>/<desc>, used <style>
  // rules, and IDs referenced by url(#…)/CSS selectors/<use>. Deterministic.
  svg?: boolean          // Default: true
  png?: PngEncoderOptions
  webp?: WebpEncoderOptions
  avif?: AvifEncoderOptions
}

interface PngEncoderOptions {
  // Any option accepted by sharp(...).png() is forwarded; these are the common knobs.
  compressionLevel?: number    // 0 (fastest/largest) – 9 (slowest/smallest). Default: 9.
  effort?: number              // 1 (fastest) – 10 (slowest/smallest). Default: 10.
  adaptiveFiltering?: boolean  // Adaptive row filtering.
  palette?: boolean            // Quantise to a palette (lossy) to shrink flat-colour PNGs.
  quality?: number             // Palette quality when palette is enabled, 1-100.
}

interface WebpEncoderOptions {
  effort?: number         // 0 (fastest) – 6 (slowest/smallest). Default: 6.
  quality?: number        // 1-100. Defaults to the render `quality` option.
  lossless?: boolean
  nearLossless?: boolean
}

interface AvifEncoderOptions {
  effort?: number         // 0 (fastest) – 9 (slowest/smallest). Default: 6.
  quality?: number        // 1-100. Defaults to the render `quality` option.
  lossless?: boolean
}
```

The SVGO + Mermaid CSS-pruning pass is an internal pipeline step (`src/optimize.ts`,
not part of the package's public `exports`) wired automatically into
`renderDiagramFileToDisk()` via `config.optimize.svg`; there is no standalone
importable `optimizeSvg()` in this release. It never throws: on a pathological
document, an SVGO failure falls back to the (possibly CSS-pruned) input rather
than losing the render.

### FileOverride

```ts
interface FileOverride {
  formats?: OutputFormat[]
  theme?: Theme
  quality?: number
  scale?: number
  contrastOptimize?: boolean
}
```

### DiagramkitConfig

```ts
interface MermaidLayoutOptions {
  // 'off' = never measure. 'warn' (default) = log when ratio out of band.
  // 'flip' = retry with swapped flowchart direction. 'elk' = retry with ELK layout
  // engine + aspectRatio hint (requires @mermaid-js/layout-elk). 'auto' = try flip
  // then elk, keep the closest to target.
  mode?: 'off' | 'warn' | 'flip' | 'elk' | 'auto'  // Default: 'warn'
  targetAspectRatio?: number      // Default: 4 / 3 ≈ 1.333
  tolerance?: number              // Must be > 1. Default: 2.5
}

interface DiagramkitConfig {
  outputDir: string              // Output folder name. Default: '.diagramkit'
  manifestFile: string           // Manifest filename. Default: 'manifest.json'
  useManifest: boolean           // Enable incremental builds. Default: true
  sameFolder: boolean            // Place outputs next to source. Default: false
  defaultFormats: OutputFormat[] // Default output formats. Default: ['svg']
  defaultTheme: Theme            // Default theme. Default: 'both'
  outputPrefix: string           // Filename prefix. Default: ''
  outputSuffix: string           // Filename suffix. Default: ''
  extensionMap?: Record<string, DiagramType>  // Custom extension overrides
  inputDirs?: string[]           // Directories to scan (relative to project root). Default: scan entire tree
  overrides?: Record<string, FileOverride>    // Per-file render overrides
  mermaidLayout?: MermaidLayoutOptions        // Mermaid aspect-ratio rebalance options
  optimize?: OptimizeOptions                  // SVGO + Mermaid CSS pruning + sharp encoder tuning. Default: { svg: true }
}
```

### Manifest

```ts
type Manifest = { version: 2, diagrams: Record<string, ManifestEntry> }
type ManifestEntry = {
  hash: string
  generatedAt: string
  outputs: ManifestOutput[]
  formats: OutputFormat[]
  theme?: Theme
}
type ManifestOutput = {
  file: string
  format: OutputFormat
  theme: 'light' | 'dark'
  width?: number
  height?: number
  quality?: number
  scale?: number
}
```

## Configuration

### Config File Formats

```json5
// diagramkit.config.json5
{
  outputDir: '.diagramkit',
  defaultFormats: ['svg'],
  defaultTheme: 'both',
  overrides: {
    "hero.mermaid": { formats: ["svg", "png"], scale: 3 },
    "docs/*.excalidraw": { theme: "light" },
  },
}
```

```ts
// diagramkit.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'diagramkit'

export default defineConfig({
  defaultFormats: ['svg'],
  defaultTheme: 'both',
  overrides: {
    'hero.mermaid': { formats: ['svg', 'png'], scale: 3 },
  },
})
```

### Merge Order

1. Built-in defaults
2. Global: ~/.config/diagramkit/config.json5 (or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME)
3. Environment variables: DIAGRAMKIT_FORMAT, DIAGRAMKIT_THEME, DIAGRAMKIT_OUTPUT_DIR, DIAGRAMKIT_NO_MANIFEST
4. Local: diagramkit.config.json5 or .ts (walks up directory tree) — or explicit --config path
5. CLI flags / programmatic overrides

`optimize` is deep-merged like `mermaidLayout` — a partial override (just `svg`, or
just `png`) keeps the rest of the defaults; each layer is validated independently,
so a malformed `optimize.png` value warns and falls back rather than dropping the
whole `optimize` block.

### Output Optimization (`optimize`)

```json5
{
  optimize: {
    svg: true,                                 // SVGO + Mermaid CSS pruning. Default: true.
    png: { compressionLevel: 9, effort: 10 },  // sharp PNG encoder overrides
    webp: { effort: 6 },                       // sharp WebP encoder overrides
    avif: { effort: 6 },                       // sharp AVIF encoder overrides
  },
}
```

`svg: true` (the default) runs a curated, accessibility-preserving SVGO pass
(preserves `viewBox`, `width`/`height`, `role`/`aria-*`/`<title>`/`<desc>`, kept
`<style>` rules, and every id referenced by `url(#…)`/CSS/`<use>`; disables
`cleanupIds`, `inlineStyles`, `removeUnknownsAndDefaults`, `removeDesc`,
usage-based CSS removal) plus a reference-aware pruning pass for Mermaid's
`<style>` boilerplate (Mermaid embeds ~21 KB of classes per SVG, most matching
nothing in that particular diagram). Both run once, before the SVG is written to
disk and before it is rasterized, so PNG/WebP/AVIF are converted from the same
optimized source. `png`/`webp`/`avif` merge on top of diagramkit's tuned sharp
defaults; any option `sharp(...).png()/.webp()/.avif()` accepts is forwarded, not
just the documented fields. Set `svg: false` to skip SVG optimization entirely
(e.g. hand-authored sources that need byte-exact passthrough).

### Extension Aliases

```
.mermaid, .mmd, .mmdc       → mermaid
.excalidraw                  → excalidraw
.drawio, .drawio.xml, .dio  → drawio
.dot, .gv, .graphviz        → graphviz
```

Custom overrides via config.extensionMap (merged with built-in map).

## Architecture

### Browser Pool
Single Chromium instance managed by BrowserPool:
- Lazy initialization on first render
- Reference counting with 5s idle timeout
- Launch coalescing for concurrent acquire() calls
- 4 dedicated pages: mermaid-light, mermaid-dark, excalidraw, drawio
- Page init coalescing for concurrent getExcalidrawPage()/getDrawioPage() calls
- Mermaid needs separate light/dark pages (mermaid.initialize() is global)
- Excalidraw and drawio handle dark mode per-render call
- Singleflight IIFE bundle cache builds prevent duplicate rolldown work
- Graphviz uses Viz.js/WASM directly (no browser needed)
- Process cleanup on SIGINT/SIGTERM

### Manifest System
SHA-256 content hashing for incremental rebuilds:
- Per-directory .diagramkit/ folders contain manifest.json
- Format accumulation: re-processing regenerates all previously generated formats
- Staleness checks: hash mismatch, format change, theme change, or missing output files
- Orphan cleanup removes outputs for deleted source files
- Missing outputs trigger re-render even if hash matches

### Dark Mode Contrast
postProcessDarkSvg() optimizes dark SVG readability:
- Scans inline fill color attributes
- Computes WCAG 2.0 relative luminance
- Darkens high-luminance fills (>0.4) to lightness 0.25
- Preserves hue and saturation
- Applied to all four engines (mermaid, excalidraw, drawio, graphviz) when contrastOptimize is enabled

### Watch Mode
Uses chokidar for file watching:
- Per-file debounce (200ms)
- Render mutex prevents concurrent manifest writes
- Failed renders leave output/manifest untouched
- Returns cleanup function to stop watching

## Testing

```bash
npm test           # All tests
npm run test:unit  # Unit tests only (fast)
npm run test:e2e   # E2E rendering tests (requires build)
npm run typecheck  # Type checking
npm run validate   # Full validation (lint + typecheck + build + tests)
```
